3.      PUBLIC HEARINGS


        a)   BYLAW NO. 1919
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 596, (City Centre Pedestrian), Bylaw
             No. 1919, 2021''

                                                                                                       July 19, 2021
                                                                                                        Page 2 of 22




Acting iVIayor Stewart opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1919 at 5:34 pm.

Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Bylaw No. 1919 proposes to amend Zoning Bylaw
No. 300 as follows:


    •   To amend the existing City Centre 1 Zone to establish a 6-storey height limit;
    •   To create a new City Centre 2 Zone that would only permit multi-family residential land uses and
        include a height limit of 4 storeys;
    •   To create a new City Centre Pedestrian Zone that would include provisions for mandatory
        commercial space and allow for higher density development; and
    •   To amend the City Centre design guidelines to include a map indicating where these zones may be
        considered as part of rezoning applications as well as additional policies to aid with the
        interpretation of the map.

This is being proposed in order to help clarify and implement Council's long-term vision with respect to
redevelopment within the City Centre.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

Acting Mayor Stewart called a first time for presentations.

L. Plomp. 3592 Whimfield Terr - Proposal should have more community input about 25 or 30 storey
buildings.

J. Gintaut. 1331 Ravensview Dr - Not enough time between Agenda publishing and Public Hearing for
residents to be informed. Concern that Mayor and Council do not consider residents' opposition. Concern
about the height of buildings being proposed. Concerns about traffic, parking, desires of residents, and
community development.

Acting Mayor Stewart called a second time for presentations.

No presentations.

Acting Mayor Stewart called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, she declared the Public
Hearing for Bylaw No.1919 closed at 5:42 pm.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

    1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per lot
         prior to subdivision approval:

              a. $660 towards the Affordable Housing Fund; and
              b. $3,960 towards the General Amenity Fund.

    2.   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority
         of all other charges on title, that agrees:

              a.   That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the
                   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to subdivision approval or the issuance of a
                   building permit, whichever is first:

                        i.   Full frontage improvements; and
                       ii. A storm water management plan;

              b.   That a Construction Parking and Traffic Management Plan be provided to the satisfaction of

Acting MayorStewart called a first time for presentations.

B. Davidson and M. Hobbs. 880 Walfred Rd - Both support the application. It is appropriate and the
infrastructure is adequate. Sewers are needed for failing septic fields.

A. Baker. 2670 Winster Rd - In support of the development. Agood place for young families.

J. Robilotti. 3440 Mvles Mansell Rd - Support the development.

S.Laface. 842 Cuaulta Cres - Will sewers be coming up to the area?

Acting Mayor Stewart - Replied to the caller that yes, the sewers will be extended.

Acting Mayor Stewart called a second time for presentations.

M. Rogers. 2711 Winman Lane - Oppose the cumulative impact this of development. Full development will
impact the wildlife corridor. What assessments have been done?

L Stohmann replied to caller - The developer will be required to provide an assessment at the time of
development approval.

G. Lewis. 860 Walfred Rd - Very intense development and construction is causing traffic issues. Could a
lower density development be more appropriate? Local standard of living is reduced with density.

C. Harder, 844 Goldstream Ave - Development is too much for the area. Families would be dependent on
vehicles or infrequent bus service. Lots would be eligible for secondary suites, requiring more parking.
What transportation plans are being considered?

L. Stohmann replied to caller - Secondary suites would require more parking.

M. Mahovlich replied to caller - Master traffic/ transportation plans are up to date. Long term plan is in
place and roads are being built out.

L. Plomp. 3592 Whimfield Terr - Developer has several ongoing projects. Developers should have a
requirement to complete projects. Huge projects have huge traffic impacts. The public is unaware that
there is a master traffic plan.

T. Dawson. 894 Walfred Rd - Development is appropriate, need sewers to be extended. Due to the
housing shortage this development is needed.

Acting Mayor Stewart called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, she declared the Public
Hearing for Bylaw No. 1969 closed at 6:02 pm.

                                 for the use by individuals in each unit, as required by Bylaw
                                 300 and designated accordingly, and that the parking stalls are not
                                 sold or rented out individually;
                           V.    That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking
                                 spaces, shall feature an energized outlet capable of providing
                                 Level 2 charging or higher to the parking space; and
                                      1. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric
                                          vehicle charging;
                                      2. Where an electric vehicle energy management
                                          system is implemented (load sharing), the Director of
                                          Engineering may specify a minimum performance
                                          standard to ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
                                      3. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle
                                          Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in operation and the Strata
                                          Council may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant
                                          from installing the EV charging equipment.
